payload.task_text:
I need a summary of overall student grades across all courses. For each course, query the learning management system for that course's enrollments with grades, and use each enrolled student's **current overall grade** — the `current_score` field inside each enrollment's grade record. Ignore enrollments that have no grade or a null `current_score`.

Create an Excel file called Canvas_Grade_Summary.xlsx with two sheets.

The first sheet, named "Grade Summary", should have exactly one row per course, with these columns in this order: **Course** (the course name), **Students_Graded** (the number of students in the course whose `current_score` is present/non-null), **Avg_Score**, **Max_Score**, and **Min_Score**. Avg_Score, Max_Score, and Min_Score are the average, maximum, and minimum of those students' `current_score` values, each rounded to 2 decimals. Sort the rows by Avg_Score descending.

The second sheet, named "Summary", should contain a header row with columns `Metric` and `Value`, followed by three rows: **Total_Courses** (the total number of courses), **Highest_Avg_Course** (the name of the course with the highest Avg_Score), and **Overall_Avg_Score** (the unweighted average of the per-course Avg_Score values across all courses, rounded to 2 decimals).

Also record these three summary metrics (Total_Courses, Highest_Avg_Course, Overall_Avg_Score) in a Google Sheet titled "Grade Summary Report" for the academic team to review.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, read every required score row but cap each sub-agent's raw Canvas input at four pages. Return only partial aggregates and never hard-code runtime course or page counts.

The main agent calls `canvas_list_courses(include_ended=true)`, validates unique course IDs/codes/full names, and issues one native-parallel discovery batch with `canvas_get_course_grades(course_id=<literal ID>, page=1, per_page=1, type=["StudentEnrollment"])` for every returned course. Take `total_count` from pagination, compute `pages_at_100=ceil(total_count/100)`, and freeze one literal `{course_id,course_code,course_name,total_count,pages_at_100}` row per course. For each course, divide its consecutive page interval `1..pages_at_100` into non-overlapping consecutive work items of at most four pages; freeze every work item as `{course_id,course_code,course_name,total_count,page_start,page_end}` and verify their union is the complete page manifest. The current runtime manifest must fit one Wave of at most 128 items; if it does not, use the minimum number of additional consecutive waves required by the 128-agent cap without changing any item.

1. Wave 1 — after the work-item manifest is frozen, dispatch exactly one explore sub-agent per item in one parallel response, never more than 128. Render the wave as numbered lines, N from 0:

   1. explore 0 (enterprise-data-analyst 0): Page-chunk owner for frozen work item 1. It receives that item's complete literal `{course_id,course_code,course_name,total_count,page_start,page_end}`. In its first tool-call response it issues the one-to-four independent `canvas_get_course_grades(course_id=<literal ID>, page=<each integer page_start..page_end>, per_page=100, type=["StudentEnrollment"])` calls natively in parallel. It verifies the returned pages equal that exact interval and every page reports the frozen `pagination.total_count`. From `enrollment.grades.current_score`, ignore nulls and return only `{course_id,course_code,course_name,total_count,page_start,page_end,pages_observed,returned_rows,graded_count,score_sum,score_min,score_max,duplicate_pages,missing_pages}`. Do not return enrollment IDs, score lists, or raw rows, and do not modify Canvas.
   2. explore 1 (enterprise-data-analyst 1): Page-chunk owner for frozen work item 2 — same literal recipe, only that item's identity substituted.
   ...
   K. explore K-1 (enterprise-data-analyst K-1): Page-chunk owner for frozen work item K — same literal recipe, only that item's identity substituted. If K>128, keep this numbering across the minimum number of consecutive waves of at most 128.

After the page-work Wave(s), the main agent requires exactly one compact record per frozen work item, rejects missing/duplicate pages, verifies every course's summed `returned_rows` equals its discovery `total_count`, and combines unrounded partials into a canonical course table `{course_name,students_graded,avg_score,max_score,min_score}`. Round course values only after combining unrounded sums, sort by Avg_Score descending with course name ascending for ties, and compute Total_Courses, Highest_Avg_Course, and the unweighted average of per-course rounded Avg_Score once.

2. Wave 2 — dispatch exactly 2 coder sub-agents in parallel:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): One Coder is the sole writer of Canvas_Grade_Summary.xlsx in the dynamically resolved task workspace. Create exactly Grade Summary and Summary with the exact headers, canonical rows and literal values; read both populated ranges back.
   2. coder 1 (external-workflow-operator 0): One Coder is the sole owner of the Google spreadsheet titled Grade Summary Report. Create the spreadsheet once, write only the header plus the three canonical summary rows to the exact range A1:B4, and read A1:B4 back. Do not add diagnostic cells or any extra data range.

The main agent finally verifies both outputs against the same canonical metrics. No raw grade page, extra verification agent, or hidden expected value may be introduced.

You are a read-only data-extraction agent working against a Canvas LMS instance. Do NOT create, modify, or delete anything. Only read. ASSIGNMENT (format COURSE_ID|COURSE_NAME|PAGE_RANGE): 12|Data-Driven Design (Spring 2014)|1-7 Parse it as: course_id = the integer before the first "|"; course_name = the text between the first and second "|"; assigned page range = "A-B" after the second "|", inclusive. GOAL: For each page in your assigned range, extract exact statistics about that page's enrollment grade records. TOOL: `mcp__canvas__canvas_get_course_grades`. Call it with course_id set to your course id, per_page set to exactly 100, and page set to the page number. Do NOT pass any type[] or enrollment_state[] filters. Each response contains: - `enrollments`: a list of records. Each record has `type`, `role`, `enrollment_state`, and a `grades` field. `grades` is either the empty object {} or an object with `final_score`, `current_grade`, `current_score`. - `pagination`: with `page`, `per_page`, `total_count`, `total_pages`, `has_more`. PROCEDURE: 1. Call page 1 first. Read `pagination.total_pages` and `pagination.total_count`. 2. Your assigned range may include page numbers greater than total_pages. Skip those (do not call them) and list them under PAGES_SKIPPED. 3. For every assigned page number P with 1 <= P <= total_pages, call the tool for page P and compute: - R = number of enrollment records returned on page P - SCORED = the list of `current_score` values from records where `grades` is a non-empty object AND `grades.current_score` is not null. Use `current_score`, never `final_score`. Include a record regardless of its `type`/`role`/`enrollment_state`; the ONLY exclusion rule is a missing or null `current_score`. - n_scored = number of values in SCORED, n_empty = R - n_scored - sum = exact arithmetic sum of SCORED - min and max = smallest and largest value in SCORED (use NA if SCORED is empty) ACCURACY IS CRITICAL - the sum must be exact. Recommended method: build a frequency table of the distinct `current_score` values on the page (value -> count), verify the counts add up to n_scored, convert each distinct value to integer hundredths (round(v*100)), multiply by its frequency, and add those integers. Report sum = that integer total divided by 100. Recompute at least once to confirm. Take your time; correctness matters far more than speed. OUTPUT - reply with EXACTLY this plain-text block and nothing else (no prose before or after, no raw JSON, no code fences): COURSE_ID: COURSE_NAME: TOTAL_COUNT: TOTAL_PAGES: ASSIGNED_PAGES: PAGES_SKIPPED: DATA: page=

records= n_scored= n_empty= sum= min= max= Rules for the DATA lines: one line per page actually processed, in ascending page order; every field present on every line; if SCORED is empty use sum=0 min=NA max=NA; do not round, truncate, or summarize; do not omit any page. Extract per-page Canvas grade stats
